Why this exists

Being watched is the default.

{# Two columns so the diagram sits beside the claims instead of below them: the section was a heading and a wide figure stacked, which left the right half empty for the whole scroll. #}
{# The problem, as a picture: one wire, everything on it legible to whoever holds it. Deliberately drawn before any prose -- the diagram IS the paragraph the first version wrote out longhand. #} {# Two rows: the problem, then what the network does about it. The second row shows the RENDEZVOUS shape rather than a simple relay chain, because "hide your server" is a different claim from "hide the visitor" and only the two-sided picture makes it. Each end builds its own hops to a meeting point, so neither side ever learns the other's address and no single hop sees both ends. Deliberately simplified: hop counts are illustrative, and the drawing says nothing about traffic timing, which is where this protection actually ends (Constitution s7). Static SVG -- the live canvas is in the hero above, and the include binds to fixed ids so a second instance would be inert. #} {# Three claims, one line each. The first version spent a paragraph on each of these and said no more than the line does. #}

It is not about hiding

Reading about a diagnosis. A search term that is evidence where you live. A source who needs your silence to be worth something.

No one owns it

Unrelated operators, unrelated places. No company to subpoena, no server to seize, no one who can be leaned on for the whole picture.

A crowd, or nothing

Anonymity used by a few is a spotlight. It only protects you when it is ordinary — which takes people, not cryptography.
